That is one of the biggest misconceptions in Marvel lore. Doctor Doom can actually take his mask off whenever he wants, and the real reason he refuses to is way more twisted.

In his classic origin (later refined by John Byrne to bridge Jack Kirby’s and Stan Lee’s takes), Victor’s college lab accident actually left him with just a small scar but his monstrous vanity couldn't stand even a tiny imperfection. Out of pure ego and impatience in Tibet, he forced the monks to place his newly forged iron mask onto his face before it finished cooling, burning and hideously disfiguring himself for real!

Despite the myth that it’s permanently fused to his skin, Doom constantly upgrades his armor and takes the mask off in private. He’s even unmasked in front of others (like surgeon Donald Blake in The Mighty Thor #182), had it pulled off by Scott Lang, and even walked around completely unmasked after Reed Richards healed his face following Secret Wars!

Magneto literally yanks the mask inches off his face here before Doom’s green magic snaps it back, proving it’s sorcery and pride keeping it on, not fused skin! 

The mask isn’t a physical prison. Doctor Doom keeps it on by choice because his ego is bigger than any scar underneath it.

posts.text:
Kelis said Nas hit her so many times during their marriage that she was covered in bruises, and she walked out on him seven months pregnant with his son.

The day after she gave birth, a judge ordered Nas to pay her $44,000 a month, and Kelis admitted she didn't just take it: "Did he hit me? Mhm. Did I hit him back? Mhm."

Kelis stayed quiet for nine years. Then she sat down with Jason Lee on Hollywood Unlocked: "I have edited myself for nine years and I woke up this morning and said, not today."

She called the marriage dark. "There was a lot of drinking. There was a lot of mental and physical abuse." She says Nas drank so much he blacked out, "He'll never admit it," and that she never started the fights: "I'm not afraid to throw a punch, but I wouldn't have started it."

The moment it hit her was February 2009, when the photos of Rihanna's beaten face after Chris Brown went around the world. "I remember so clearly when the pictures came out... I had bruises all over my body."

Two months later, seven months pregnant, she filed for divorce. She says the baby is the only reason she left: "Had I not been pregnant, I probably would have stayed longer. Because I really did love him."

Then the money war started. Kelis's lawyers told the court Nas was making $244,826 a month and had close to $11 million in the bank, but wasn't paying her or the baby anything.

The judge ruled the day after their son Knight was born: $44,000 a month. By December it went up to $51,000 a month, more than $600,000 a year. Nas also had to pay $155,787 of her legal fees, and later he pleaded not guilty to contempt of court over $200,000 in support he hadn't paid.

When the interview came out, Nas and his team didn't answer a single request for comment.

The Fed held rates. Bitcoin still couldn't catch a break

On October 28, the Federal Reserve kept rates unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%. But the 10-2 vote revealed a split: two policymakers actually wanted another 25 bps hike

$BTC briefly bounced above $81K after the announcement, but the optimism didn't last. By October 30, Bitcoin had slipped below $77K as broader risk-off sentiment hit crypto and tech stocks

So what did we learn?

A rate pause is not the same as monetary easing. Inflation remains elevated, economic activity is strong, and the Fed has not ruled out another hike in December

The market wanted relief. It got a timeout

Now the next big question is whether the Fed can afford to tighten again without putting even more pressure on risk assets

🇮🇶 Thousands of Kurds are protesting Baghdad's move to take control of their oil and borders...

Iraq's PM Ali al-Zaidi wants the federal government to manage Kurdish border crossings, approve oil exports and take over oil fields in 4 provinces.

He says it's about stopping oil smuggling, and Iraq's Supreme Court has backed the move.

But Kurdish leaders say it violates their constitutional rights, with rival Kurdish parties now coming together against Baghdad.

Oil is a huge part of this fight. It accounts for roughly 90% of Iraq's budget.

For Baghdad, it's about control. For the Kurds, it's about protecting the autonomy they've had since 1991.

Source: AP / Writer: Daniyal

A Forbes analysis proposes transferring 50-60 retired American F-15C/D Eagles to Ukraine to strengthen its defenses against Russian aerial attacks.

The U.S. currently has over 240 of these fighters in storage. Maybe, refurbishing existing aircraft could provide a faster alternative to waiting years for newly manufactured F-16s, Gripens or Rafales.

The proposal would also free up Ukraine's existing fighters for other military missions.
